GRAND RAPIDS, MI -- Police say the homicide of a 34-year-old woman on Grand Rapids Community College's campus was a random act of violence that occurred after the suspect tried to befriend the victim.

Jeanne Lyn Huntoon, of Muskegon, was found stabbed and assaulted to death near shrubs and bushes on the campus about 2:47 a.m. Saturday, April 30. A witness reported seeing a man dragging her body in the 100 block of Bostwick Avenue NE, between the parking ramp and a building.

Marcus Lamar Bivens, 19, of Grand Rapids, was arrested Sunday and is held on a count of open murder. He is expected to be arraigned Tuesday.

Grand Rapids Police Sgt. Terry Dixon said investigators believe Bivens encountered Huntoon about 2:30 a.m. outside the parking ramp. They spoke for a few minutes before he allegedly produced a knife and stabbed Huntoon. He beat her when she was on the ground, then dragged her body a short distance, police said.

Police don't believe the incident stemmed from a robbery. Bivens and Huntoon did not know each other. The details of their brief conversation are not known, but police believe he tried to befriend her.

"We are still looking into all evidence as to what was behind the actual killing itself," Dixon said, regarding a possible motive. "We do believe that this was a random act of violence."

Surveillance cameras were helpful in determining "some of the movement that took place" during the incident, but video footage did not show the entire encounter, Dixon said.

Neither Huntoon nor Bivens have current ties to the college. Huntoon was accepted to GRCC as a student in 2004 but never attended classes, Dixon said.

Bivens was leaving a downtown business when he encountered Huntoon on campus. Dixon said police don't know where Huntoon was heading.

A tip from a citizen was critical in arresting Bivens. Investigators on Sunday received information naming him as a suspect in the homicide, and a flyer with his information was distributed within the department.

An officer who had prior contact with Bivens at Lookout Park located him Sunday night near the park in the 700 block of Fairview Avenue NE.

Bivens agreed to be questioned at the police department. Dixon said investigators obtained evidence from Bivens.

"Also, he did provide statements that only the suspect in that homicide would know," Dixon said. "We do believe that he did place himself at that murder scene, and we have since charged him with open murder."

Community college police were not patrolling the campus at the time of the killing. The school is on break between semesters. Commencement was held Friday night.

GRCC issued an email alert Saturday morning.

State police records show Bivens has prior felony convictions of receiving and concealing stolen property, breaking and entering a building with intent, and assaulting/resisting/obstructing police. Prior to the homicide, he was arrested and released April 20 in Grand Rapids on a misdemeanor related to disorderly conduct, according to jail and state police records.

Dixon said there are more than 20 reports of Bivens being a juvenile runaway.
